knowledge_refs.formula_empty_justification: The distance follows directly from wavelength as the distance travelled by a wavefront in one oscillation; no registered major formula is applied.

hints: One oscillation produces one wavelength of travel by a wavefront.
Multiply the distance for one oscillation by the N oscillations.
walkthrough: In one oscillation, a wavefront moves one wavelength, λ.
For N oscillations, it moves N copies of this distance.
The distance moved in time t is Nλ.

ai_rubric.observable: States that the distance moved by the wavefront is Nλ.

hints: Frequency f is the number of oscillations completed in one second.
Use the duration of one oscillation and multiply it by N.
walkthrough: One oscillation takes one period, T = 1/f.
The loudspeaker completes N oscillations in the stated time, so t = NT.
Substituting T = 1/f gives t = N/f.

ai_rubric.observable: States that the time for N oscillations is N/f.

hints: Wave speed is the distance travelled by a wavefront divided by the time taken.
Substitute the two expressions found for N oscillations, then cancel common factors.
walkthrough: Wave speed is distance divided by time: v = distance / time.
From part (i), the wavefront travels Nλ in the time N/f.
v = Nλ / (N/f) = Nλ × f/N = fλ.
Therefore the wave equation is v = fλ.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses the distance Nλ and time N/f to deduce v = fλ.

hints: Measure one complete cycle horizontally, for example from one crest to the next crest.
Convert the horizontal length to a period using the time-base setting, then take the reciprocal.
walkthrough: One complete cycle occupies 4.0 cm horizontally on the CRO trace.
The period is T = (4.0 cm)(0.20 ms cm⁻¹) = 0.80 ms = 8.0 × 10⁻⁴ s.
To two significant figures, the frequency is 1.3 × 10³ Hz.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses the 4.0 cm horizontal cycle width and 0.20 ms cm⁻¹ time-base setting to obtain T = 0.80 ms or 8.0 × 10⁻⁴ s.

knowledge_refs.formula_empty_justification: Coherence is assessed as a definition of the phase relationship between two waves; no major formula is applied.

hints: Compare the relative phase of the two sound waves as time passes.
walkthrough: Coherence concerns the phase relationship between two waves.
For coherent waves, this phase difference does not drift with time.
Coherent waves therefore maintain a constant phase difference.

ai_rubric.observable: States that coherent waves maintain a constant phase difference.

knowledge_refs.formula_empty_justification: The minimum-loudness phase relation is a qualitative destructive-interference condition; no registered major formula is applied.

hints: At a minimum loudness, the waves arrive in antiphase and cancel.
walkthrough: A minimum in sound loudness is produced by destructive interference.
For destructive interference, a crest of one wave arrives with a trough of the other wave.
The waves are therefore 180° out of phase.

ai_rubric.observable: States a phase difference of 180° for the minimum-loudness position.

hints: At X the paths are equal, so the path difference is zero; count the intervening maxima to find the interference order at Y.
Use the path difference at Y together with S₂Y = 7.40 m to find the longer S₁Y path.
walkthrough: At X, S₁X = S₂X, so the path difference is zero and the detector is at a maximum loudness position.
Y is the second subsequent maximum-loudness position, so its constructive-interference path difference is 2λ.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses a path difference of 2λ at Y, equivalently S₁Y − S₂Y = 2λ.
Uses S₂Y = 7.40 m and λ = 0.85 m to obtain S₁Y = 9.1 m.
